subject: Orphaned records: access / deletion request and provenance handoff
messages:
From: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmehealth.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: data-protection@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: access + deletion for orphaned user email (evidence + roles)

Hi Ben,

We discovered a set of legacy records tied to a decommissioned product that include PII for a small cohort of users (example: user_id 8d9f4c, email: test.user+archived@acmehealth.com). Under our DPA / GDPR obligations we need: (1) a full export of any user content Redwood holds for those identifiers, (2) confirmation of deletion (with a deletion manifest and provenance logs), and (3) clarity on whether Redwood acts as controller or processor for this dataset.

For context: these records appear to be generated by our integration from 2019–2021. Acme will initiate a subject-access and erasure request to the user; we need Redwood's deliverables to complete our evidence bundle for the regulator. Please advise next steps and timeline.

I've attached a short CSV listing the affected IDs.

Thanks,
Sophie
Data Requests Lead
Acme Health

[Attachment: acme_dsr_manifest_20270328.csv (CSV, 9KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access + deletion for orphaned user email (evidence + roles)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the details and the manifest. We can support both an export and deletion confirmation, but need to clarify responsibilities and the exact scope before we proceed. Quick summary of next steps from our side: 

- We will confirm whether the records in question were persisted as part of hosted inference inputs/outputs or as support logs/metadata. That distinction determines the export format and retention path.
- Karthik (privacy engineering) will map controller vs processor responsibilities based on the integration and the DPA.
- We'll produce an export bundle and a deletion certificate with provenance logs where possible; note that for certain ephemeral caches we may only have aggregated traces rather than full payloads.

Can you confirm: (A) Are you submitting the formal DSAR on behalf of the end user today? (B) Do you need the export in a particular schema or a simple CSV + JSON blobs is acceptable?

Tentatively we can provide an initial status and ETA within 48 business hours once we verify the record locations. Attaching an internal checklist we will use to map evidence items.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: export_and_provenance_checklist.md (TXT, 3KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access + deletion for orphaned user email (evidence + roles)

Forwarding my mapping for the thread — sending to Sophie once Ben confirms. Long answer short: Redwood is primarily a processor for customer-provided payloads stored/served via the hosted API. The customer (Acme) is the controller for the user-level content you send to our APIs. Exceptions and nuances below: 

- Hosted API request/response payloads: processor. We persist model inputs/outputs only according to your tenancy settings and DPA — typically customer-controlled retention. We will export full payloads if they are present in persistent storage.
- Support logs & internal observability events: may contain identifiers (redacted by default). Where support captured raw payloads to triage incidents, we have a documented process to pull those artifacts; these are treated as data for which Redwood acts as a processor but may have retention governed by our incident response policy.
- Account metadata (account owner contact, billing contact): controller responsibilities are shared per contract (we process billing info as a service provider).

Action items I propose: 
1) I will run a targeted search across the tenant shard for the IDs you provided and produce an export bundle (CSV index + JSON payloads) and provenance log (append-only actions showing timestamps and service IDs).
2) Laura (privacy ops) will assemble a deletion certificate indicating which stores were purged and include cryptographic checksums where available.
3) Neha (legal) will confirm the DPA clause references and include SCC references and a short note on remedial steps if regulators require additional proof.

ETA: initial export + preliminary provenance notes by 2027-03-30 17:00 UTC. Full deletion certificate by 2027-03-31 EOD depending on downstream jobs.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Privacy Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Deliverables enclosed: 
- Export bundle (CSV index + JSON payloads) — Drive link: https://drive.redwood.company/AcmeHealth/DSR-Exports/2027-03-29
- Deletion certificate (signed) indicating permanent wipe from object store and purge job id purge-job-77a9
